title: Family Cyber Defense
intro: Glitch is always looking for the weakest lock in the house. Let's lock down the basics that protect your whole family!

questions.prompt: I'll just give my best friend my password—

choices.text: That's fine, best friends can be trusted
choices.coach: Knight Rule number two! Passwords are secret — even from your best friend.

choices.text: Keep it secret, even from your best friend
choices.coach: Friends can change, and passwords can leak. Secret means secret!

choices.text: Share it but change it later
choices.coach: Once it's shared, you can't take it back — best to never share it.

questions.prompt: Pixel! It's me, Shieldy! Send me your password, quick!

choices.text: Send it, Shieldy needs it urgently
choices.coach: The real Shieldy would NEVER ask for a password. Asking + hurrying = trick.

choices.text: Say no — no one ever needs your password
choices.coach: Locked! Not even friends or trusted grown-ups ever need your actual password.

choices.text: Send half of it to be safe
choices.coach: There's no safe way to share part of it — just don't send any of it.

questions.prompt: What's a family code word for?

choices.coach: It's a real safety tool, used to check that someone really is who they say they are.

choices.text: Checking who someone really is in a surprise call or message
choices.coach: Exactly right — this matters even more now that voices can be copied by computers.
You can use it any time you need to check — it's not a one-time thing.

questions.prompt: Something online felt weird, but I don't want to get in trouble for telling my parent.

choices.coach: You are never in trouble for telling a grown-up something felt wrong.
Exactly the Knight move. Telling is never punished in a Knight family.

choices.text: Only tell if it happens again
choices.coach: Tell the first time — don't wait.

questions.prompt: Should all your accounts use the same password?

choices.text: Yes, one password is easier to remember
choices.coach: If one gets found out, every account with that same password is now at risk too.

choices.text: No — different passwords for different accounts
choices.coach: Exactly right — this keeps one problem from becoming five problems.

choices.text: Only use it twice, not more
choices.coach: Even twice is risky — give each account its own password.

questions.prompt: Final Knight Rule: what's the golden rule of Family Cyber Defense?

choices.coach: The goal is using the internet safely, not avoiding it completely.

choices.text: Passwords are secret, code words check who's real, and telling a grown-up is always safe
choices.coach: Shield up! That's the whole castle wall right there.

choices.text: Only trust people you've met once in person
choices.coach: Even people you've met can pretend to be someone else online — good habits matter more than one meeting.
